judgments.note: Appeal of ZBA decisions (municipal). One of the three decisions concerns a permit application for a single-family dwelling on a parcel with a fire-damaged commercial diner: either new construction or a conversion creating housing, so new housing even though the NOV and wall parts are not.

The housing application is one of three subjects (with a wall application and an NOV), and the court notes it is unclear whether the diner would be remodeled or replaced; either way a dwelling unit is created where there was a commercial building.
One single-family dwelling; not a replacement of housing (the existing building was a commercial diner).
No subdivision is mentioned, but the documents never state that none is proposed, so unknown per the lots rule.
ZBA upheld incompleteness rulings (and the NOV); an incompleteness ruling is 'other', so the appellant seeks 'other'.

Most documents call it Marc Wood's appeal; one later order says 'the Woods appealed', but Susan Wood did not participate below or at trial, and Docket 1-1-11 is the Town's enforcement action (no appellants), so only Marc Wood is listed.

The Statement of Questions (as listed in the summary judgment order) turns on whether permits and engineering certification/technical review were required, discontinuance of a nonconforming use, NOV validity and enforceability of a cost policy: fixed rules, facts and legal questions, not evaluative standards.

No explicit 'de novo' phrase, but the court held a three-day evidentiary trial with a site visit, made its own findings on the applications and itself deemed them incomplete; no on-the-record procedures mentioned.
Applications deemed incomplete rather than denied on the merits, but later orders say the court 'denied the applications' and the diner building was later ordered removed; no authorization observed.

Supreme Court affirmed 2013 and the court calls the matters resolved/closed; later post-judgment contempt proceedings (through March 2020) enforce the judgment rather than review the municipal decision.

Start: filed August 17, 2010 (exact, June 2018 recusal order). End: judgment final August 12, 2013 after affirmance (June 14, 2013) and denial of reargument. If post-judgment proceedings counted, the end would be on or after 2020-03-26. Person ruling: post-judgment proceedings do not extend the duration.
The cease-development and removal injunctions were relief granted to the Town in enforcement Docket 1-1-11 Vtec (per the post-judgment decisions), so not attributed to this docket.
1-1-11 Vtec decided jointly; Supreme Court appeal docket number not given; prior Wood dockets about the same parcels are named.
